newsitem.title: HONG KONG: FOCUS - HK's Hang Seng Index sets sights on 15,000.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - HK's Hang Seng Index sets sights on 15,000.

text.p: Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index staged a furious rally into new record ground on Friday with its sights clearly set on 15,000 points ahead of Hong Kong's return to Chinese rule. Hong Kong's blue chip Hang Seng Index scored its biggest point gain since January, surging 341.24 points, or 2.37 percent, to close at a record high of 14,757.81.
Turnover was the second highest ever at HK$18.74 billion.

"There is no doubt that sentiment is pretty strong heading into the handover," said Howard Gorges, vice chairman of South China Holdings. "It is beginning to look as though 15,000 to 16,000 is the target range for the handover."

Friday's surge -- the biggest since the index gained 472.78 points on January 15 this year -- was linked to active futures-related activity, brokers said. The June contract on the Hang Seng Index contract jumped 380 points to 14,860. "Investors are positive on the market in June," said Geoff Galbraith, institutional sales trader at NAVA SC Securities.
Shares in HSBC Holdings Plc led the rise with a surge of HK$7.00 to an all-time high of HK$235.00.

Red chips -- Hong Kong-incorporated companies with financial backing from China -- were also a focus, with market newcomer Beijing Enterprises Holdings Ltd staging a stunning second-day performance with a gain of HK$5.00 to HK$45.20.
The company, controlled by Beijing's municipal government, ended its market debut on Thursday at HK$40.20 compared with an issue price of HK$12.48.
As Hong Kong heads into its final month as a British colony, investors are scrambling to pick up China-related plays, boosting sentiment and liquidity, brokers said.
"Hong Kong is being flooded with liquidity from China, the region and local money," said Antony Mak, sales director at Vickers Ballas. "People are stacking up on red chips."
With Hong Kong's real estate market showing signs of a pick-up following a slowdown when the government imposed measures to cool down prices in late March, analysts said the outlook was rosy.
"Everything in the garden is doing good," said Gorges.
But analysts said some consolidation may lie ahead before the Hang Seng Index challenges 15,000 points.

"It has climbed more than 2,000 points in about a month. It is time for the market to digest its gains before another rally by the end of June," said Kelvin Tang, an analyst at ImPac Asset Management.
But as Hong Kong's handover to Chinese rule approaches, sentiment is expected to remain buoyant. The territory returns to Chinese rule on midnight of June 30.

"I am sure there is going to be a burst of enthusiasm before the handover. It would not surprise me to see the market remaining pretty good up until the handover," said Robert Rountree, regional strategist at Nomura Research Institute.
"But after that you could very easily see a consolidation and it could be a sharp one. People are always going to start locking in some profits," he said.
